newsitem.title: UK: UK watchdog urges BT to cut internet school bill.
newsitem.headline: UK watchdog urges BT to cut internet school bill.

text.p: British telecoms watchdog Don Cruickshank on Wednesday called on the industry to offer lower flat-rate charges for schools to use the "information superhighway".
Cruickshank welcomed the cable industry's move to allow schools unlimited access to the internet computer network via ISDN lines that offer high-speed, digital communications.
But he said British Telecommunications Plc should cut its ISDN2 prices for schools to around 750 stg per year for unlimited use and 250 stg for connection.
"Schools are so obviously a special case. There are great benefits to them being on line.

"It is now up to BT to respond," he said at the launch of a report by a special task force to advise on ways of dismantling the telecoms obstacles preventing schools, colleges and libraries using superhighway services.
